matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Compute the integer values of both sides, determine the numeric difference, and search for a single‑stick move that changes a numeral or operator by exactly that amount (or its opposite) while keeping all symbols valid Roman numerals or operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Use this as a first step when the equation is false and the imbalance is small enough that a single‑stick change could correct it.
matchstick.example: In "IX = XVII + IX", the RHS exceeds the LHS by 17; moving the vertical stick from the plus sign to the numeral "XVII" (creating an extra I) and turning the plus into a minus reduces the RHS by 17, yielding a correct equality.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and a V appears, relocate one of V’s diagonal sticks so the two sticks cross, turning V into X and increasing that numeral’s value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase a numeral by 5 and a V is present.
matchstick.example: Changing "V" to "X" in "V + I = VI" balances the equation.

matchstick.title: Change + to - and add I
matchstick.principle: When converting a plus sign to a minus sign, move the vertical stick of the plus sign to a numeral; the minus sign remains, and the transferred stick creates an extra I, increasing that numeral by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the RHS is too large and reducing it by turning + into – (subtracting twice the added operand) plus adding 1 to a numeral balances the equation.
matchstick.example: In "IX = XVII + IX", moving the vertical stick from “+” to “XVII” makes it “XVIII” and turns “+” into “–”, yielding a correct equality.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: If a numeral contains more than one I, you can remove one I (a vertical stick) from it and add that stick as a new I to another numeral, decreasing the first value by 1 and increasing the second by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is an even number (or any integer) and there are at least two I’s in the equation.
matchstick.example: Moving an I from "XII" to the left operand of a subtraction changes "XII = XI - XI" into "XI = X - XI".

matchstick.title: Change - to = by adding a horizontal stick from a numeral
matchstick.principle: If a minus sign appears and you need to increase the RHS, take a horizontal stick from a numeral that can spare one (e.g., a V or X) and attach it to the minus sign, turning it into an equals sign while the source numeral loses a horizontal component but remains a valid numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the RHS is too low and converting “-” to “=” adds the missing value.
matchstick.example: Turning "XI - I" into "XI = I" by moving a horizontal from "V" to the minus sign.

matchstick.title: When converting - to +, also move a vertical stick to form a valid plus sign
matchstick.principle: To change a minus sign into a plus sign you must supply a vertical stick; take it from a numeral that can lose an I without becoming invalid, and attach it to the minus sign, creating a plus sign while the source numeral loses one I.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the RHS is too low and turning “-” into “+” (adding the second operand) would fix the equation, but you need the missing vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Converting "XI - IX" to "XI + IX" by moving an I from "XII" to the minus sign.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: Move one horizontal stick from the equality sign to the minus sign; the equality becomes a minus and the minus becomes an equality, effectively swapping their roles while using only one stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When swapping the positions of “-” and “=” could balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Changing "XII = XI - XI" into "XII - XI = XI".

matchstick.title: Ensure a valid '=' remains when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: If you relocate a stick from the equality sign, you must simultaneously create a new equality sign elsewhere (or swap with another operator) so that the equation still contains a valid “=” after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a solution proposes moving a horizontal stick out of “=”, verify that a new “=” is formed.
matchstick.example: In "XII = XI - XI", moving a horizontal from “=” to the minus sign without creating a new “=” would be invalid.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and an X appears, reposition one of X’s diagonal sticks so the two sticks form a V shape, turning X into V and decreasing that numeral’s value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to reduce a numeral by 5 and an X is present.
matchstick.example: Changing "X" to "V" in "X + I = VI" balances the equation.

matchstick.title: When converting + to -, move its vertical stick to form an I
matchstick.principle: To change a plus sign into a minus sign, remove the vertical stick of the plus sign and attach it as a new I to a numeral; the plus becomes a minus, and the numeral gains one unit.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the RHS is too large and reducing it by turning “+” into “–” (subtracting the second operand) plus adding 1 to a numeral (by the transferred stick) exactly balances the equation.
matchstick.example: In "IX = XVII + IX", moving the vertical stick from “+” to “XVII” creates “XVIII” and turns “+” into “–”, yielding a correct equality.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any numeral can donate a stick, overlooking that X and V consist solely of angled sticks; removing one leaves an invalid shape.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before moving a stick, check that the source numeral still forms a valid Roman numeral after the removal; only numerals with removable I’s (multiple I’s) or X→V transformations are allowed.

matchstick.description: Providing an incomplete equation after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on numeric balance and forgets to keep all characters present, sometimes deleting a symbol entirely.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that every original character (numeral or operator) still appears as a valid symbol; the equation must remain syntactically complete.

matchstick.description: Changing – to + without adding the required vertical stick (resulting in an incomplete plus sign)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model changes the minus sign to a plus sign by adding a horizontal line but neglects the necessary vertical component.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When converting “-” to “+”, always source a vertical stick from a removable I or from the plus sign itself, ensuring the plus sign is complete.

matchstick.description: Using an angled stick as a vertical stick (or vice versa), creating an invalid numeral or operator
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats sticks as interchangeable, ignoring orientation constraints.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Respect stick orientation: diagonal sticks can only form V or X; vertical sticks only form I or the vertical part of +; horizontal sticks only form – or =.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid '=' sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a horizontal from “=” without compensating, resulting in a lone minus sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: If a stick is taken from “=”, either swap it with another operator (e.g., turn “-” into “=”) or add a horizontal elsewhere to recreate a valid “=” sign.
